text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make the code cleaner and easier to understand, which improves readability for everyone on the team. When developers refactor, they might rename variables, break large functions into smaller ones, or remove duplicate logic. The behaviour of the program stays exactly the same, so users do not notice any difference. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes and messy code are left for later. Although it takes time, regular refactoring keeps a project healthy and makes future changes easier and safer.
